name: Papular Xanthoma

criteria.description: Presence of multiple yellow to orange papules primarily on the trunk and extremities
Skin biopsy showing foamy histiocytes and Touton giant cells without lipid metabolism abnormalities
Normal serum lipid levels excluding hyperlipidemia-associated xanthomas
No evidence of systemic disease or malignancy associated with xanthomas

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical lesions with confirmatory histopathology and normal lipid profile
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other xanthomatous disorders and systemic lipid abnormalities.

laboratory: Normal serum lipid panel (cholesterol, triglycerides within reference ranges)
imaging: Not typically required; imaging usually normal
other: Skin biopsy demonstrating foamy histiocytes and Touton giant cells without systemic lipid abnormalities

distinguishingFeatures: Sudden onset of crops of papules
Lesions often on buttocks and extensor surfaces
Typically occurs in infants and young children
Solitary or few nodules rather than multiple papules
Histology shows different giant cell types

redFlags: Rapid increase in number or size of lesions
Presence of systemic symptoms such as weight loss or fever
Abnormal lipid profile suggesting secondary causes
references: Bolognia JL, Schaffer JV, Cerroni L. Dermatology. 4th ed. Elsevier; 2018.
James WD, Berger TG, Elston DM. Andrews' Diseases of the Skin. 13th ed. Elsevier; 2019.
